reject_reason: other: invalid evidence - the headline ra_core_singleblock rows time dead code. In experiments/2026-9-1_family-productionization/bench_release.c every call passes raw_stream=NULL, and ra_core_singleblock (src/ra_core/c/ra_core.c) returns cons, which always equals the key, so no generated word is observable. With the helpers force-inlined, the 255-step serial output loop can be removed by the compiler; the README's own table shows ~0.00 ns/word generate time and a real time (0.191 ns/word x 255 = 48.7 ns) below the separately timed init (49.96 ns). The rows that do consume output (orbit --stream, whose ra_reseed reads the swapped L[]) are 3.2x slower than xoshiro256** (3.87 vs 1.20 ns/word) and level with scalar Philox (3.89).

The valid first-party rows show no win over xoshiro256**.

corrections.caveats: The singleblock benchmark discards every output (raw_stream=NULL; the function returns the key), so the 20 GB/s figure times init plus call overhead, not generation; a 255-step serial dependency chain cannot run at ~0 ns/word. The README's 2026-09-12 'fairness fix' (always_inline on the singleblock helpers) moved singleblock from ~8000 to ~20000 MB/s, consistent with the compiler deleting the now-dead loop. Orbit, which does generate, is 3.2x slower than xoshiro256** on a long stream. An earlier 30303 MB/s claim was withdrawn as non-reproducible. corrections.claimed_speedup: gcc-15 benchmark JSON (2026-07-22): XoshiroSIMD fill_u64 1645 ns per 4096 values (2.49e9 values/s) vs scalar Xoshiro fill_u64 3835 ns (1.07e9 values/s), about 2.3x (derived from page data); SIMD Philox4x32 fill 7970 vs scalar 27502 ns (about 3.5x) and ChaCha20 21555 vs 61019 ns (about 2.8x) (derived from page data). Scalar Xoshiro uniform() 1.32 ns vs the same engine through std::uniform_real_distribution 4.65 ns (about 3.5x) and vs std::mt19937_64 + std::uniform_real_distribution 8.01 ns (about 6x) (derived from page data); std::mt19937_64 single u64 call 1.60 ns vs scalar Xoshiro 0.94 ns. docs/benchmarks.rst: Xoshiro bulk 'reaches ~2.3x its scalar loop'; uniform() ~1.6 ns vs ~5.2 ns, 'roughly 3x' (a different run).
corrections.caveats: The gain is for bulk fills only: single-value SIMD calls cost 2.82 ns vs 0.94 ns for scalar Xoshiro (buffered read overhead, per the docs), so one-at-a-time use should stay scalar. The SIMD stream interleaves SIMD_WIDTH xoshiro256++ lanes, lane i being the scalar generator after i jump() calls (tests/test_xoshiro_simd.cpp checks each lane against the scalar engine, which tests/test_xoshiro.cpp checks against Vigna's xoshiro256plusplus.c), so it is the same generator but a different output order than one scalar stream for the same seed. The std::mt19937_64 figure is a per-call time, not a bulk fill. Shared GitHub-hosted runner; cpu_model.txt is rewritten on each publish run. libstdc++ inferred from gcc-15 on ubuntu-24.04. License is BSD-3-Clause with an added acknowledgement clause (SPDX BSD-3-Clause-Attribution, not OSI-approved), so marked reference although permissive. Pre-1.0, no tagged release, 3 stars.

corrections.caveats: Big speedups are in vectorial (block fill of 10,240) mode; scalar single-value V-MT19937 is about 1.7-2.1x the original reference. The README omits the 32-bit STL-MT19937 row that doc/main.tex and perf.cpp include; std::mt19937 beats the original reference from AVX2 up. On SVE256 STL-MT19937-64 (573) beats V-MT19937-64 scalar (513). README and main.tex disagree on the AVX-512 MT19937 scalar figures (README X 1341 / V 729; main.tex X 929.5 / V 1354.0) and slightly on other AVX-512 MT19937 cells, so they come from different runs. V-family output interleaves jump-separated MT states (src/test.cpp checks each against the reference at the jumped index), so it is a different sequence from one MT19937 for the same seed; the X-family is bit-identical to the reference. libstdc++ inferred from GCC 16 (main.tex credits GCC auto-vectorization of the STL MT).
